subclaims.reason: On a new connection the NIO2 IO thread runs Nio2Acceptor.java:300 handler.sessionCreated -> AbstractSessionIoHandler.java:39-44 -> SessionHelper.java:581-606 signalSessionCreated -> the listener proxy, which iterates a CopyOnWriteArraySet snapshot (EventListenerUtils.java:197), so a dispatch already in flight still invokes the timeout listener even if stop() concurrently removes it. Inside the anonymous listener's sessionCreated (AbstractFactoryManager.java:488-494, synchronized only on the listener), a non-empty tracked set triggers ensureTimeoutScheduled (:509-513), which reschedules when timeoutListenerFuture == null. Concurrently, a user thread calling SshServer.stop()/SshClient.stop() runs removeSessionTimeout as the first close step (SshServer.java:386, SshClient.java:494) -> stopSessionTimeoutListener (:526-538), which with no lock cancels the future (nulling timeoutListenerFuture at :521) and nulls sessionTimeoutListener at :535, with the executor later nulled at SshServer.java:395/SshClient.java:503. If the stop thread's nulling lands while the IO thread is inside sessionCreated, the IO thread observes timeoutListenerFuture == null and executes scheduleAtFixedRate with a null command (or on a null executor), throwing NPE on the IO thread. Nothing rules this out: the stop path takes no lock, the fields are plain non-volatile (:86-87), and snapshot iteration does not prevent in-flight invocation, so no common lock or happens-before ordering excludes the interleaving.
caveats: Needs stop()/close() on one thread concurrent with an in-flight session creation on an IO thread, with a non-empty tracked set (positive auth/idle timeout, SessionTimeoutListener.java:46-49).
Needs the stop thread's field writes visible to the IO thread in that order, which the code permits (plain fields, no ordering).

Relies on JDK scheduleAtFixedRate throwing NPE for a null command argument, and on the NPE propagating on the IO thread through the proxy/signalSessionCreated rethrow path: platform behavior outside the tree.
